source_citation: Base-text/variant readings transcribed from R.W. Franklin's critical apparatus ('Textual Notes' field), as published in the live IIIF manifests of the Emily Dickinson Archive (Amherst College Archives & Special Collections / Houghton Library, Harvard University; curiosity.lib.harvard.edu/emily-dickinson-archive). Manifest URLs follow the pattern https://nrs.lib.harvard.edu/URN-3:HUL.EDA:W{n}:MANIFEST:3. Used under EDA's Copyright & Terms of Use (CC BY-NC-ND 3.0, https://curiosity.lib.harvard.edu/emily-dickinson-archive/about/copyright-terms-of-use), personal/non-commercial-research provision. This file supersedes data/fascicle34_hand_coding.json's variant fields, data/fascicle34_worked_example_ground_truth.json, data/fascicle34_verified_pairs_round2.json, and data/fascicle34_tei_verified_pairs.json for the purpose of base/variant pair accuracy -- those files are kept for their own record of what was known at each stage, not deleted, since the corrections and retractions along the way are themselves part of this project's own documented process.
note_on_witnesses: Where a poem exists in more than one manuscript copy, Franklin's apparatus numbers them (1), (2), (3). Different witnesses can show genuinely different base words at the same line position, not just different variants of the same base word -- these are kept distinct below, not merged.
note_on_exclusions: Franklin's apparatus also includes 'Division' notes (where a word wraps across a line break in the manuscript -- not a variant) and occasional 'Emendation' notes (an editor's correction of an apparent slip, e.g. 'thro'' for 'thro') -- neither is a variant reading and neither is included below.

poems.poem: Her Sweet turn to leave the Homestead

pairs.note: Franklin's notation gives no base-text word here, only the line number -- likely a pure addition rather than a substitution for an existing word.

poems.poem: Pain- has an Element of Blank
Promise This- When You be Dying
poems.note: Witness 2 shares the same lines 15-16 and 27 with alternate readings ('Bliss', 'scarce') per the apparatus's 'alt (2)' notes, but Franklin's own notation leaves the base-text side blank for witness 2 at line 15-16 -- not confidently reconstructable as a clean pair, left out rather than guessed at.
